 Match Awards from Germany’s magical 5-0 win over the Netherlands
 The Klopp era is well underway as Germany cruise past the Dutch.
 by Jack Laushway Updated Nov 16, 2026, 11:01 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 (Photo by Odd ANDERSEN / AFP via Getty Images) AFP via Getty Images Part Of Germany’s November 2026 International Break: All Updates see all updates Jack Laushway Since the 2006 FIFA World Cup in Germany, Jack has been a passionate diehard fan of both Die Mannschaft and Bayern Munich ever since. After being a longtime reader of BFW, he became a contributor on the site officially in 2020. After moving to Germany, Jack experienced the sport from many different perspectives and communities, only deepening his love for the sport. While Germany and Bayern matches have remained at the core of his coverage, these experiences have given him a unique angle to his conversations. The Canadian-born writer has travelled to Austria, Spain, Germany, and Bermuda to cover football stories with his unique perspective. Jack is also a running-host on Bavarian Podcast Works. Germany are so back. In a troubling scenario heading into this match, Germany required all three points to have any chance of qualifying for the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals. In what was supposed to be a tightly contested match, Jürgen Klopp found some magic in his new squad scoring five against a Netherlands side that just came off a 7-0 thrashing of a solid Greek side.
 Jersey Swap: No one
 This one always feels harsh giving out but simply no one stood out from the pack in this Dutch side. What was actually a decent start for Xavi’s side in the first half was squandered by some missed scoring chances that really should have been put in the net. Thankfully for Germany, the Dutch were simply not clicking in this one.
 Der Kaiser: Nico Schlotterbeck
 While Nico Schlotterbeck might not have that illustrous aerial presence that Malick Thiaw offers, the Dortmund defender certainly showed off his heading with a brilliantly placed goal. Schlotterbeck was reliable defensively and offers much more going forward than other defenders.
 While Germany’s defense was never going to be the storyline of this match, it was ruthlessly efficient in thwarting anotherwise excellent Dutch attack, as shown in recent matches.
 Fussballgott: Joshua Kimmich
 The midfield was arguably the weakest side of the German team in this game and yet there was no bad performance to be found. Aleksander Pavlović and Kimmich were perhaps equally effective in this match and did a great job at picking up on the mistakes of a shaky Dutch performance.
 While many were disappointed to not see the recent duo of Tom Bischof and Pavlović share the midfield over this international break, it is clear that Kimmich and Pavlović are the main cast for the time being.
 Der Bomber: Florian Wirtz
 The Liverpool star did as he has done best in recent years, turning up for the German national team. While Wirtz was perhaps outshined by a certain winger by the end of the match, it was he who got things going for the Germans in the second half and created the momentum that they would ride for the rest of the match.
 Wirtz is the face of this team and Klopp is going to build something special around their star.
 Meister of the Match: Brajan Gruda
 The RB Leipzig talent delivered once again with a great display on the right wing. While things weren’t clicking early for the winger, he found his groove in the second half causing all sorts of problems for the Netherlands defenders.
 This guy is the real deal and it is no wonder why Gruda has been on the radar of the national team in the past. The 22-year-old is propelling himself into a full blown star over the last few months.
 What do you think about the awards? Who else do you think deserved a shout? Let us know in the comments!
